evidence.section: 2 Methods of Processing and Characterization
evidence.quote: The investigated alloy specimens were prepared by arc-melting of the pure elements. The processing of arc melted ingots (AMI) involved preparation of binary eutectic alloys of Ti70.5Fe29.5, and Ni91.2Zr8.8, followed by alloy additions such as, Sn or Al to achieve the desired compositions.

evidence.section: 3.3 Deformation Mechanism of Nano-lamellar Eutectic Composites
evidence.quote: Figure 5a shows the formation of profuse slip bands in the b-Ti and FeTi lamellae phases, aligned at an angle of 90 and 45–55 in FeTi and b-Ti, respectively.

evidence.section: 3.3 Deformation Mechanism of Nano-lamellar Eutectic Composites
evidence.quote: The presence of high-density slip lines all over the microstructure and dislocation pile-ups at the b-Ti/FeTi or c-Ni/Ni5Zr lamellae interfaces indicate that dislocation slips and their pile-ups are the major source of work hardening in the NECs.

evidence.section: 3.3 Deformation Mechanism of Nano-lamellar Eutectic Composites
evidence.quote: It has been observed that the Sn addition has changed the lattice parameter of b-Ti without altering the lattice parameter of FeTi, which was also confirmed by EDS analysis under transmission electron microscope [ 15]. Therefore Sn preferentially dissolves in b-Ti without bringing any change to the structure of FeTi.
